concepts.name: Fock states
concepts.statement: The eigenbasis of the field Hamiltonian is formed by the number states, or Fock states, each holding a definite number of photons in its mode.

concepts.name: Single-mode description
concepts.statement: Many properties of quantum fields can be understood from the evolution of a single mode, which is also quantitatively right for atoms in the field of a high finesse cavity.

concepts.name: Photon statistics
concepts.statement: The probability distribution for the number of photons in a mode, the diagonal of the field's density matrix in the Fock basis.

concepts.name: Single-mode thermal state
concepts.statement: A single mode in thermal equilibrium has a diagonal density matrix whose photon distribution falls exponentially with n, so zero photons is most likely, the mean is the Bose-Einstein n̄, and the mean field vanishes.

concepts.name: Multimode thermal light
concepts.statement: Summed over many modes, each most likely empty, a thermal field's total photon number is most likely finite and its distribution looks Poissonian; sunlight shows single-mode statistics only when filtered to a bandwidth Δω and detected in gates shorter than 1/Δω.

concepts.name: Coherent state
concepts.statement: The eigenstate |α⟩ of the photon annihilation operator, the quantum state of the classical coherent field of a laser, with a well-defined mean electric field.

concepts.name: Coherent amplitude
concepts.statement: The eigenvalue α of a coherent state: the mean field is proportional to it and the mean photon number is |α|².

concepts.name: Quadrature operators
concepts.statement: In analogy to position and momentum of an oscillator, x̂ and p̂ are the Hermitian combinations of â and â†; the field is x̂ cos ωt + p̂ sin ωt, so they are its in-phase and out-of-phase components.

concepts.name: Minimum uncertainty of a coherent state
concepts.statement: A coherent state has quadrature variances of 1/2 each, the most classical the uncertainty principle δxδp ≥ 1/2 allows; in phase space it is a disc of diameter √2 at a distance √2|α| from the origin.

concepts.name: Local oscillator
concepts.statement: A reference field cos ωt mixed with a signal, against which x̂ gives the in-phase and p̂ the out-of-phase component.

concepts.name: Shift operator
concepts.statement: The operator D̂(α) = exp(αâ† − α*â) displaces a state in the x̂, p̂ plane; acting on the vacuum it makes the coherent state, whose Fock expansion follows from the identity for exponentials of operators with c-number commutator.

concepts.name: Poisson statistics of a coherent state
concepts.statement: The photon number of a coherent state follows a Poisson distribution with variance equal to its mean |α|², so for large fields the intensity grows better defined.

concepts.name: Coherent state from a classical dipole
concepts.statement: A classical oscillating dipole driving the field evolves the vacuum by the shift operator, so the field it radiates is a coherent state with α = id₀E₀t/2ℏ.

concepts.name: Multimode coherent state
concepts.statement: A product of coherent states in every mode, whose mean field is the classical field with Fourier components E_k ∝ α_k.

concepts.name: Overcompleteness of coherent states
concepts.statement: The coherent states resolve the identity, (1/π)∫d²α|α⟩⟨α| = 1, but are not orthogonal, |⟨α|β⟩| = e^{−|α−β|²/2}, so they form an overcomplete set.

concepts.name: Quasi-probability distribution
concepts.statement: The density operator written as ∫P(α)|α⟩⟨α|d²α; P(α) always exists, gives normally ordered expectation values as a probability would, but can be negative.

concepts.name: Nonclassical states of light
concepts.statement: Negative values of P(α) are associated with non-classical properties of the field and mark a boundary between quantum and classical states.

concepts.name: Linear optical transformations
concepts.statement: Effects independent of the incident power, such as phase shifts and beamsplitters, under which a coherent state stays coherent; a phase shift takes â to âe^{iφ}.

concepts.name: Beamsplitter transformation
concepts.statement: A lossless beamsplitter with transmission t and reflection r mixes the two input annihilation operators linearly and unitarily (|r|² + |t|² = 1), so two coherent inputs leave as coherent states.

concepts.name: Beamsplitter as coupled oscillators
concepts.statement: The beamsplitter transformation is the unitary exp(iθâ₁â₂† + iθâ₂â₁†) of two coupled harmonic oscillators, θ set by t and r.

concepts.name: Cavity quantum electrodynamics
concepts.statement: A single atom confined in a high finesse cavity interacting with its single mode, an intrinsically anharmonic medium for the quantum field.

concepts.name: Jaynes-Cummings model
concepts.statement: The coherent coupling of a two-level atom to one resonant cavity mode in the rotating frame: absorbing a photon raises the atom, and the atom's relaxation emits one.

concepts.name: Jaynes-Cummings dynamics
concepts.statement: The Hamiltonian couples each pair |2⟩|n⟩, |1⟩|n+1⟩ alone, which oscillates at g√(n+1); the general solution sums these pairs.

concepts.name: Vacuum Rabi oscillations
concepts.statement: An excited atom in an empty cavity exchanges its excitation reversibly with one photon in a well-defined mode at the vacuum Rabi frequency g, unlike spontaneous emission into a continuum.

concepts.name: Strong coupling regime
concepts.statement: The regime in which the atom-cavity coupling g dominates dissipation: an excited atom gives its energy to the cavity mode faster than it emits into free space, g² > γκ.

concepts.name: Rabi oscillations in a coherent field
concepts.statement: Replacing √(n+1) by √n̄ for a coherent field leaves the field coherent and gives classical Rabi oscillations of the atom with period about 1/(g|α|).

concepts.name: Collapse of Rabi oscillations
concepts.statement: The photon number spread δn makes each Fock component's phase g√(n+1)t differ; once gtδn/√n̄ reaches unity, about t ∼ 1/g, they dephase and the Rabi oscillations damp out.

concepts.name: Revival of Rabi oscillations
concepts.statement: At longer times the phase corrections of the dominant Fock states reach multiples of π and the oscillations revive, imperfectly, at about 2π√n̄/g, a generic feature of isolated quantum nonlinear systems.

concepts.name: Field splitting in the Jaynes-Cummings model
concepts.statement: A coherent field interacting with the atom splits into two coherent components rotating in opposite directions in phase space, entangled with the atom, so the field no longer stays coherent.

concepts.name: Schrödinger cat state
concepts.statement: A superposition of two macroscopically distinguishable coherent states such as |iα⟩ ± |−iα⟩, with exponentially small classical coherence but higher order quantum coherence, easily destroyed by decoherence.

concepts.name: Beamsplitter model of loss
concepts.statement: Loss is a beamsplitter: the signal is attenuated by t while vacuum entering the other port adds fluctuations; a coherent state |α⟩ leaves as |tα⟩, but a Fock state does not stay a Fock state.

concepts.name: Cavity loss rate
concepts.statement: The rate κ at which the intracavity field energy leaks through a partially transmitting mirror, set by its transmission and the round-trip time.

concepts.name: Classical cavity field equation
concepts.statement: Counting one round trip, the intracavity field decays at κ/2 and is fed by the input field; its response is a Lorentzian of width κ, and a medium adds a polarization drive.

concepts.name: Input-output relation
concepts.statement: The output field of a cavity is the reflected input field plus the transmitted cavity field.

concepts.name: Quantum cavity mode equation
concepts.statement: Replacing the cavity field by â and adding the noise that goes with the decay gives a Heisenberg-Langevin equation: â decays at κ/2 and is driven by a noise operator.

concepts.name: Microscopic model of cavity loss
concepts.statement: Mirrors couple the cavity mode to continuum modes â_k with coefficients t_k; with Ŝ = â this is the spontaneous emission model, and the Wigner-Weisskopf approximation gives the decay rate κ = 2π|t_k|²D(ν) and the noise operator.

concepts.name: Cavity noise operator
concepts.statement: The cavity noise is the outside field leaking in through the mirror, the input field; in a thermal environment of n photons its correlators are (n+1)κδ(t−t′) and nκδ(t−t′).

concepts.name: Master equation of a damped cavity
concepts.statement: With Ŝ = â the general master equation describes cavity loss and its fluctuations, equivalent to the Heisenberg-Langevin description.

concepts.name: A coherent state in a lossy cavity
concepts.statement: A coherent cavity field decaying into vacuum stays coherent, |αe^{−κt/2}⟩: its mean decays while the quadrature variances stay 1/2.

concepts.name: Loss washes out nonclassical states
concepts.statement: Whatever the initial state, cavity loss drives the quadrature variances to 1/2, so squeezed and other nonclassical states lose their nonclassical coherence; generating them competes with dissipation.

concepts.name: Cavity mode driven by atoms
concepts.statement: Atoms in the cavity add a driving term to the mode's Langevin equation, the quantum analogue of the medium's polarization; for many atoms and strong fields this Heisenberg-Langevin approach is nearly classical, while for few photons and atoms the master equation or stochastic wavefunction serves better.

concepts.name: Open and closed cavities
concepts.statement: An open cavity confines the mode in one dimension (L ≫ λ), so the atom still decays to free space at nearly its free-space rate; a closed cavity confines the field in three (L ∼ λ) and can strongly suppress spontaneous emission.

concepts.name: Master equation of cavity QED
concepts.statement: The atom and cavity mode together form the system: Jaynes-Cummings evolution with the cavity detuned by δ, cavity loss at κ and atomic decay to free space at γ.

concepts.name: Dressed states of the Jaynes-Cummings ladder
concepts.statement: Each pair |1⟩|n⟩, |2⟩|n−1⟩ is a two-level system coupled by g√n and diagonalized on its own into dressed states; decay couples the manifolds and broadens them.

concepts.name: Vacuum Rabi splitting
concepts.statement: Probed in reflection, a resonant atom-cavity system shows its lowest dressed states as two peaks split by twice the coupling, 2g, the vacuum Rabi splitting.

concepts.name: Collective enhancement
concepts.statement: With N atoms at the cavity antinode the coupling grows to g√N and the vacuum Rabi splitting to 2g√N; classically, the atoms’ dispersion shifts the cavity resonance.

concepts.name: No-jump dynamics of cavity QED
concepts.statement: Starting from |2⟩|0⟩, only |1⟩|1⟩ is coupled coherently; with the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian of cavity loss and atomic decay the no-jump amplitudes evolve exactly, and for g ≫ γ, κ they show weakly damped vacuum Rabi oscillations.

concepts.name: Purcell effect
concepts.statement: When the cavity is overdamped, g < κ, eliminating the photon amplitude modifies the atom's decay rate and Lamb shift; in an open cavity at zero detuning the decay is enhanced by 4g²/κ.

concepts.name: Quality factor
concepts.statement: The cavity decay rate is the mode frequency over the quality factor Q.

concepts.name: Cavity finesse
concepts.statement: The finesse F is the mean number of times a photon circulates before leaking out; the photon lifetime 1/κ is F times the round-trip time.

concepts.name: Coupling to a cavity mode
concepts.statement: The atom-cavity coupling g grows with the dipole moment and falls as one over the square root of the mode volume.

concepts.name: Figure of merit for strong coupling
concepts.statement: The ratio g²/κγ is independent of the atom, ∼ (λ²/d²)F with d the mode diameter, largest for small cavities with high reflectivity; it is the chance that the atom meets the photon before the photon leaves.

concepts.name: Suppressed decay in a closed cavity
concepts.statement: In a closed cavity γ = 0 and the atom decays only through the cavity, at a rate strongly suppressed when the cavity is far detuned, by the quality factor when V ∼ λ³.

concepts.name: Microwave cavity QED with Rydberg atoms
concepts.statement: At microwave frequencies closed cavities are possible, γ ∝ ω³ is small and g ∝ √ω, and circular Rydberg states with large dipoles and second-long lifetimes give the highest ratio of coherent evolution to decoherence, provided thermal photons are removed.

concepts.name: Single photons on demand
concepts.statement: An excited emitter strongly coupled to a cavity emits one photon into the cavity mode’s direction, a bound-to-free problem whose wavepacket envelope decays at 2g²/κ; a three-level atom can shape it, and the process is coherent and reversible.

concepts.name: Hanbury-Brown-Twiss setup
concepts.statement: Splitting a signal on a beamsplitter onto two detectors measures joint probabilities: a single photon never registers on both at once.

concepts.name: Second-order correlation function
concepts.statement: The normalized intensity correlation g⁽²⁾ of the field at two points and times, which factorizes for coherent states and is sensitive to a higher order coherence than a laser's classical coherence.

concepts.name: Bunching and antibunching
concepts.statement: g⁽²⁾(0) is 1 for a coherent state, 2 for a thermal state (bunching) and 0 for a single photon (antibunching).

concepts.name: Noise of a linear amplifier
concepts.statement: A linear amplifier of gain σ > 1 adds noise from spontaneous emission that keeps the commutators fixed, so, as the no cloning theorem demands, a quantum state cannot be amplified without losing information.

concepts.name: Degenerate optical parametric oscillator
concepts.statement: Parametric down-conversion in a cavity at half the pump frequency, so both generated fields are the one cavity mode, driven by its own conjugate with gain β set by pump and χ⁽²⁾.

concepts.name: Phase-dependent amplification
concepts.statement: In the normal modes E₁ ± E₁* one is amplified and the other de-amplified at rate β̃, so the gain depends on the field's phase relative to the pump.

concepts.name: Quantum degenerate down-conversion
concepts.statement: For a strong classical pump and large detunings the Heisenberg-Langevin equations of a cascade atom in the cavity eliminate adiabatically to dâ/dt = −iβ*â†, the classical equation with E → â, from the effective Hamiltonian of photon-pair absorption and emission.

concepts.name: Non-degenerate down-conversion
concepts.statement: Two phase-matched modes amplified together obey dâ₂/dt = −iβ*â₁†, from an effective Hamiltonian that creates and destroys photons in pairs, one in each mode.

concepts.name: Photon pairs from down-conversion
concepts.statement: From the vacuum, non-degenerate down-conversion makes |vac⟩ + ξ|1,1⟩ + ξ²|2,2⟩ + …: correlated pairs from spontaneous emission for ξ < 1, stimulated emission and squeezing for ξ ≫ 1.

concepts.name: Correlated photon numbers
concepts.statement: Each down-converted mode alone is thermal, yet the photon-number difference of the two is exactly zero, far below the shot-noise limit n₁ + n₂ of a beam divided on a beamsplitter.

concepts.name: Heralded single photons
concepts.statement: Detecting a photon in one down-converted mode heralds precisely one in the other.

concepts.name: Post-selection
concepts.statement: Conditioning all later measurements on detecting both photons of a probabilistically generated pair, so that a polarization-entangled state is used only when it was made and not lost.

concepts.name: Squeezed state
concepts.statement: A degenerate down-converter amplifies one phase-weighted quadrature and attenuates the other, so a coherent state's variances change in opposite directions while their product stays 1/4; from the vacuum it holds only even photon numbers.

concepts.name: Squeezing in a damped cavity
concepts.statement: Cavity loss adds decay κ/2 and vacuum noise to each quadrature, so the squeezed variance approaches κ/2(κ + 2β̃) instead of zero.

concepts.name: Steady-state squeezing
concepts.statement: Below threshold, β̃ < κ/2, the intracavity variances reach steady values and squeezing is at most 50% at threshold, limited by vacuum leaking in; above it the undepleted-pump analysis fails.

concepts.name: Squeezing in the output field
concepts.statement: By the quantum input-output relation the reflected vacuum and the transmitted cavity field interfere, so at threshold and zero frequency the output quadrature is perfectly squeezed, over a Lorentzian of width ∼κ relative to the standard quantum limit.

concepts.name: Homodyne detection
concepts.statement: Mixing the signal with a strong local oscillator of phase φ on a 50/50 beamsplitter and subtracting the two photocurrents measures the signal's quadrature P_φ, amplified by the oscillator amplitude.

concepts.name: Squeezed light in interferometry
concepts.statement: With squeezing parameter r the quadrature noise falls to e^{−2r}/2, so the smallest measurable phase falls to e^{−r}/√n; in practice a stronger coherent field gives a similar gain more easily.

concepts.name: Spin squeezing
concepts.statement: For N polarized spin-½ atoms the collective spin's orthogonal projections fluctuate at the atom shot noise; interactions can squeeze one projection below it at the expense of the other.

concepts.name: Atom-photon correlations
concepts.statement: N-atom Raman scattering has the form of non-degenerate down-conversion between the photon mode and the collective spin, so detecting the photon heralds an entangled atomic excitation.

concepts.name: Mean photon number
concepts.statement: The average number of photons in a mode, the mean of its photon distribution: the Bose-Einstein mean for a thermal state, |α|² for a coherent state.
